[[File:Tropical projective plane.svg|thumb|Conventional visualization of the tropical projective plane, with projection of the real coordinate axes.]]
In [[tropical geometry]], a '''tropical projective space''' is the tropical analog of the classic [[projective space]].

== Definition ==
Given a [[Module (mathematics)|module]] {{math|''M''}} over the [[tropical semiring]] {{math|'''T'''}}, its projectivization is the usual projective space of a module: the [[quotient space (linear algebra)|quotient space]] of the module (omitting the additive identity {{math|'''0'''}}) under scalar multiplication, omitting multiplication by the scalar additive identity 0:{{efn|As usual, scalar multiplication of any vector by 0 yields the identity for vector addition {{math|'''0'''}}, so these must be omitted or all vectors will be identified.}}
:<math>\mathbf{T}(M) := (M \setminus \mathbf{0})/(\mathbf{T} \setminus 0).</math>

In the tropical setting, tropical multiplication is classical addition, with unit real number 0 (not 1); tropical addition is minimum or maximum (depending on convention), with unit [[extended real number]] {{math|∞}} (not 0),{{efn|{{math|∞}} can be interpreted as either positive or negative infinity, depending on convention.}} so it is clearer to write this using the extended real numbers, rather than the abstract algebraic units:
:<math>\mathbf{T}(M) := (M \setminus \boldsymbol{\infty})/(\mathbf{T} \setminus \infty).</math>

Just as in the classical case, the standard {{mvar|n}}-dimensional tropical projective space is defined as the quotient of the standard {{math|(''n''+1)}}-dimensional [[coordinate space]] by scalar multiplication, with all operations defined coordinate-wise:{{sfn|Mikhalkin|2006|p=6|loc=example 3.10}}
:<math>\mathbf{TP}^n := (\mathbf{T}^{n+1} \setminus \boldsymbol{\infty})/(\mathbf{T} \setminus \infty).</math>
Tropical multiplication corresponds to classical addition, so tropical scalar multiplication by {{math|''c''}} corresponds to adding {{math|''c''}} to all coordinates. Thus two elements of {{tmath|\mathbf T^{n+1} \setminus \boldsymbol{\infty} }} are identified if their coordinates differ by the same additive amount {{math|''c''}}:
:<math>(x_0, \dots, x_n) \sim (y_0, \dots, y_n) \iff (x_0 + c, \dots, x_n + c) = (y_0, \dots, y_n).</math>
